narr: Extremely heavy rainfall associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ida overspread northeast New Jersey during the evening of September 1 and continued through the early morning hours of September 2. Rainfall totals ranged from 5-8+ inches across much of the region, with much of that rain falling in just a few hours. The ASOS at Newark Airport recorded 8.44 inches of rain, while the ASOS at Teterboro Airport recorded 7.14 inches. A COOP observer in Harrison recorded 8.72 inches of rain. This resulted in widespread flash flooding leading to numerous road closures and water rescues in addition to extensive river flooding. Eight people died as a result of the flash flooding and one person remains missing.
ev: The Hackensack River at River Vale exceeded its minor flood stage of 5.5 feet at 11:30pm EDT. The river then continued to rise quickly, surpassing moderate flood stage (6.5 feet) by 12:15am EDT September 2nd and major flood stage (8.0 feet) by 12:30am EDT. The river then crested at a height of 11.05 feet at 4:00am EDT September 2nd. After falling through much of the morning, the river experienced a secondary crest of 10.73 feet at 3:45pm EDT September 2nd. The river did not fall back below flood stage until 11:45am EDT on September 3rd.||The crest of 11.05 feet is the third highest on record at this location behind crests of 12.26 feet in August 2011 and 12.19 feet in April 2007.

A 66 year old man and his 46 year old daughter died as a result of flooding after going into the basement of their home on Lincoln Place in Irvington to secure it as the Elizabeth River began to overflow.

The Pascack River at Westwood rose above its minor flood stage of 5.0 feet at 9:45pm EDT. It then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (6.0 feet) by 1:00am EDT September 2nd and major flood stage (6.5 feet) at 3:15am EDT. The river crested at a height of 7.42 feet at 5:15am EDT September 2nd. The river receded throughout the morning, falling back below flood stage at 11:15am EDT September 2nd.

A car carrying two Seton Hall University students was overcome by flood waters on Main Avenue near Benson Avenue in Passaic. The body of one of the students, a 21 year old man, was later found in Newark after being swept down the Passaic River.

A car carrying two Seton Hall University students was overcome by flood waters on Main Avenue near Benson Avenue in Passaic. The body of one of the students, an 18 year old woman, was later found in Kearny after being swept down the Passaic River.
An unidentified person died by electrocution as a result of flooding in Essex County.
One person died at a hospital in Bergen County after pushing their car through flood waters and suffering a medical event.
All lanes were closed in both directions on North Avenue between Kapkowski Road and McLester Street in Elizabeth due to flooding.

Seven people were injured when the roof of the U.S. Postal Service's bulk mail facility on Harrison Avenue in Kearny collapsed due to heavy rain. 300 people were inside at the time. There were also multiple roads in the area with significant flooding.
The Fire Department was responding to a report of basement flooding endangering and electrical panel on Hamilton Avenue in Glen Rock.

The Hackensack River at New Milford rose above its minor flood stage of 6.0 feet at 11:15pm EDT. It then continued to quickly rise to moderate flood stage (8.0 feet) by 1:30am EDT September 2nd. The river ultimately rose above major flood stage (10.0 feet) at 5:00am EDT before cresting at a height of 11.03 feet at 9:15am EDT September 2nd. Thereafter the river gradually receded, falling below flood stage at 7:30am EDT September 3rd.||The crest of 11.03 feet is the third highest on record behind crests of 12.36 feet in April 2007 and 11.45 feet in September 1999.
Barbour Street in Haledon was closed due to flooding.

The Third River at Bloomfield rose above its minor flood stage of 6.0 feet at 8:10pm EDT. The river then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (8.0 feet) at 8:45pm EDT and major flood stage (9.0 feet) at 9:05pm EDT before cresting at a height of 10.14 feet at 11:30pm EDT. After cresting, the river quickly fell back below minor flood stage by 3:45am EDT September 2nd. The crest of 10.14 feet is the highest on record for this location, exceeding the previous record crest of 9.97 feet in September 1999 due to Hurricane Floyd.
Water rescues were ongoing for several occupied stranded cars on Route 17 near Racetrack Road in Ho-Ho-Kus.
Significant flooding was occurring on the ground level of Terminal B at Newark Airport. Flooding was occurring on the baggage level as well.
All eastbound lanes of US22 were closed due to flooding near the Garden State Parkway in Union.
Basement and garage flooding were reported in Livingston.
Significant flooding was reported on 20th Avenue in Paterson with several cars submerged.
Prospect Avenue, Old Hook Road, and Broadway were all closed due to flooding and cars with occupants trapped.

A 55 year old man was found dead on Ridgewood Road in the vicinity of Berkeley Road in Maplewood due to flooding. He is believed to have been swept away by flood waters while attempting to remove debris from drains in the area.
Multiple water rescues were occurring on Route 208 at Russell Avenue in Wycoff.
A water rescue was ongoing on Essex Street at the intersection with First Street in Harrison.
People were trapped in their cars in flood waters on Mill Street near the Second River in Belleville.
Multiple roads were closed due to flooding in town of Kearny including Passaic Avenue, Harrison Avenue near the Walmart, and Route 7.
EMS reported multiple water rescues ongoing across Union County due to significant flash flooding. A few evacuations were occurring as well.
Numerous water rescues were ongoing in Livingston. Rescue boats were pulling occupants to safety on Walnut Street, East Hobart Gap Road, and Old Short Hills Road.
Local roads were closed in Westwood due to flooding. Houses were flooding with water entering basements.
All southbound lanes of Jersey Avenue in Jersey City were closed due to flooding.
A water rescue was ongoing at the intersection of White Oak Ridge Road and Mohawk Road in Millburn with a vehicle stranded in flood waters.
A water rescue was ongoing for a vehicle trapped in flood waters on South Street in Newark. The occupant was on the roof of the car and the Fire Department was responding with a rescue boat.
All southbound lanes of NJ Route 17 were closed due to flooding north of Century Road in Paramus.
All were closed on US Routes 1&9 at East Grand Street in Elizabeth due to flooding.
Multiple rescues were needed across Livingston for occupied cars stranded in flood waters.
The Essex County Sheriff's Department was closing Branch Brook Park in Newark due to flooding.
All lanes of US46 were closed due to flooding between Valley Road and Clove Road in Little Falls.
The bridge at Westmore Gardens in Englewood was knocked off its foundation due to rising waters from Overpeck Creek. Two cars then crashed into the bridge.
Water was pouring into a basement through a window in Westfield.
Grand Avenue in Park Ridge was impassable due to flooding at the Memorial Drive bridge. In addition, Grand Avenue at Kinderkamack Road and Pascack Road and Mill Road were also closed due to flooding.
The intersection of McBride Avenue and Totowa Road in Totowa was closed due to flooding.

The Saddle River at Ridgewood rose above its minor flood stage of 5.0 feet at 9:30pm EDT. The river then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (6.0 feet) at 10:00pm EDT and major flood stage (7.0 feet) at 10:45pm EDT before cresting at a height of 12.01 feet at 12:45am EDT on September 2nd. The river then gradually fell overnight, eventually receding below minor flood stage again at 6:15am EDT September 2nd.
Multiple roads were flooded in Scotch Plains with multiple water rescues reported on Route 22 between Park Avenue and Glenside Avenue. Route 22 was closed.
At least 13 cars were submerged in flood waters on Cornelison Avenue in Jersey City.
Canal Street in Passaic was covered with several feet of water with water up to car roofs.
Rolling Rock Road in Mountainside was impassable due to flooding.
A car was stuck in 2.5 feet of water at the intersection of Berdan Avenue and Sunnyside Drive in Fair Lawn. Additional flooding was reported on multiple roads across the town.

The Peckman River at Ozone Avenue in Verona rose above its minor flood stage of 3.5 feet at 8:00pm EDT. It then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (4.0 feet) at 8:10pm EDT, then major flood stage (5.0 feet) at 8:25pm EDT before cresting at a height of 6.20 feet at 9:20pm EDT. The river then slowly fell over the next few hours, returning to its banks at 12:40am EDT on September 2nd.

The Saddle River at Upper Saddle River rose above its minor flood stage of 4.5 feet at 9:00pm EDT. It then continued to rise, reaching moderate flood stage (5.0 feet) at 9:15pm EDT before cresting at a height of 5.43 feet at 10:45pm EDT. This crest was the second highest on record, falling just short of the record crest of 5.64 feet in September 1999 associated with Hurricane Floyd. The river then fell back below minor flood stage at 1:45am EDT on September 2nd.

The Pascack River at Park Ridge rose above its minor flood stage of 5.2 feet at 9:15pm EDT. It then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (6.2 feet) at 9:45pm EDT and major flood stage (7.2 feet) at 11:30pm EDT. The river then crested at a height of 7.44 feet at 12:15am EDT September 2nd. The river then gradually receded overnight, falling back below minor flood stage at 4:30am EDT September 2nd.

The Rahway River near Springfield rose above its minor flood stage of 7.0 feet at 8:30pm EDT. It then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (8.5 feet) at 9:15pm EDT and major flood stage (10.5 feet) at 11:45pm EDT before cresting at a height of 10.81 feet at 1:15am EDT on September 2nd. The crest of 10.81 feet is the second highest on record, behind only a crest of 10.88 feet in August 2011 associated with Tropical Storm Irene. The river then gradually fell through the overnight hours, eventually fallign back below minor flood stage at 12:45pm EDT on September 2nd.

Four people died due to flooding at the Oakwood Plaza apartment complex on Irvington Avenue in Elizabeth. All four people were found in one apartment and included a 74 year old woman, her 71 year old husband, their 38 year old son, and a 33 year old neighbor.

The Passaic River at Dundee Dam in Clifton rose above its minor flood stage of 4.5 feet at 10:15pm EDT and crested at a height of 4.98 feet at 12:45am EDT September 2nd. The river then fell back below flood stage at 3:45am EDT on September 2nd. Flooding from the Passaic River resulted in three fatalities. A 70 year old man died when his car became stranded in 6 feet of water at the intersection of Passaic Avenue and Lackawana Place in Passaic.
An 83 year old man was found on Chestnut Street in Union Township near Overlook Hospital. He is believed to have drowned after his car got stuck and he walked out into 3-4 feet of water.
